subject: Re: Follow-up: SOC 2 / Subprocessors / Security Questionnaire
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet you and the Acme security team at a high level. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the security and procurement side.

Recap from today's discovery:
- SOC 2: you mentioned Acme requires SOC 2 instead of ISO for vendor selection; you asked whether Redwood has a SOC 2 report and what our coverage looks like (Type II, etc.).
- Data types & residency: primary concern is PII and regulated data that may be subject to GDPR/HIPAA — you asked about data flows and retention controls.
- Subprocessors: you requested our current subprocessor list and confirmation on cloud providers (and whether we share any customer-identifiable data with vendors).
- Questionnaire: you sent over the standard Acme vendor security questionnaire and asked if we can complete it.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a short subprocessor disclosure PDF (redwood_subprocessor_disclosure.pdf) and I can also share our public subprocessor page if helpful.
2) Please send the Acme questionnaire to me (or upload to the Drive link) and I'll coordinate completion with Rishi and Neha.
3) Rishi (SE) — can you please review the attached questionnaire and draft answers for the sections on network controls, encryption, and incident response?
4) Proposed follow-up: 30-min fine-grain security call with Acme's security reviewer and our security lead to walk through any gaps. Are you available Thurs 6/18 or Fri 6/19?

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_disclosure.pdf

Happy to jump on whatever works best — tagging Rishi and Neha to pick this up on the technical side.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_disclosure.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This is helpful.

Quick answers:
- SOC 2: We require vendors to have SOC 2 Type II; procurement will accept a SOC 2 report within the last 12 months. Do you have a Type II report or a timeline for when you expect one (if in progress)?
- Questionnaire: I attached Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx — if you can fill sections A–D that will get us through the initial review.
- Subprocessors: I'll also attach our expected template for subprocessor review, but a quick list of cloud providers and any analytics/monitoring vendors will suffice for now. We also need clarity on whether Redwood can access raw customer prompts or persistent storage where PII may live.

We can do Fri 6/19 10:00am PT for a security deep-dive — I'll hold the slot unless you need a different time.

Regards,
Samantha
Head of Vendor Security | AcmeCorp
[Attachment: Acme_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Acme Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today

Thanks Samantha — received the questionnaire and the time looks good.

Quick clarifications while Rishi/Neha start filling the questionnaire:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report for our control plane and inference runtime covering June 2025–May 2026. We can provide a redacted copy under an NDA / secure share link. If you need the full report, we typically provide it after an NDA and standard Acknowledgement of Receipt form.
- Subprocessors (short list): AWS (us-west-2), GCP (us-central1) for long-term storage and training infra; Cloudflare (edge/network), Sentry (monitoring/error reporting) — we do not use analytics vendors that ingest customer prompts.
- Data access: Customer prompts are processed in-memory on the serving runtime; persistent storage that contains logs/metrics is pseudonymized and ACL-restricted. We do not share raw prompts with third-party analytics vendors. Any access to request/response logs is logged and audited; we can provide a data flow diagram in the follow-up SE call.

Attachments/tools & links:
- I filled the high-level fields in your questionnaire and attached it here (acme_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf).
- Public subprocessor page: https://redwood-inference.com/security/subprocessors
- Shared drive with supporting docs and SOC 2 NDA: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cacme-security-docs

Next actions:
- Rishi / Neha: please validate answers on pages 3–7 (encryption at rest/in transit, key management, logging/retention, data deletion).
- Samantha: I'll send the NDA link and a secure report delivery once you confirm procurement's preferred NDA template.

Thanks — looking forward to the call on Fri 6/19 at 10:00am PT.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: acme_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>, Acme Security Team <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today

Looping in with updates after quick pass on the questionnaire:
- Encryption: At rest we use AES-256 with customer key options via KMS; in transit is TLS1.3. Confirmed for the questionnaire entries.
- Key management: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and have documented the process in the shared Drive.
- Logs & retention: Request/response logs are retained for 30 days by default; we have configurable retention windows per customer contract and can offer shorter retention for regulated workloads.
- Subprocessors: Confirmed list below (we'll also publish the same to the public subprocessor page):
    - AWS (data plane & storage)
    - GCP (batch processing / training)
    - Cloudflare (edge / DDoS protection)
    - Sentry (error monitoring)

Open item for Marissa: procurement asked whether we can add a clause limiting access to raw prompts to 'investigation-only' for security incidents. Can we propose a contract language option and flag it during negotiations?

I'll be on the call at 10:00am PT to walk through the technical sections.

-rishi
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
